name: Saint Maximilian Kolbe
history: A Polish Franciscan who spread devotion to the Immaculate Virgin through the press, founding a great friary and publishing house near Warsaw and a mission in Japan. Imprisoned at Auschwitz, he offered his life in place of a condemned man with a family and died in the starvation bunker. He is honoured as a martyr of charity.
life: Raymund Kolbe was born at Zduńska Wola. As a boy, he said, Our Lady showed him two crowns, one white for purity and one red for martyrdom, and he accepted both. He joined the Conventual Franciscans, taking the name Maximilian, and in Rome in 1917 founded the Militia of the Immaculata. Back in Poland, despite tuberculosis, he built Niepokalanów, the City of the Immaculata, where hundreds of friars printed magazines read across the country. From 1930 he founded a similar mission at Nagasaki. Arrested by the Gestapo in 1941, he was sent to Auschwitz. That summer, after a prisoner escaped, ten men were chosen to die by starvation. When one, Franciszek Gajowniczek, cried out for his wife and children, Maximilian stepped forward and asked to take his place. He led the others in prayer and hymns for two weeks and was killed by lethal injection on 14 August. Gajowniczek survived and was present when John Paul II canonised him in 1982.
prayerTo: Saint Maximilian, you gave your life for a stranger out of love for Christ and His Mother. Pray for all who suffer in prisons and camps, for families torn apart, and for me, that I may give myself in small ways each day, so that I am ready to give everything if God should ask. Amen.
penance: Make a small sacrifice for someone else today, giving up your place, your time or your preference, and pray for prisoners.
meditation: Hatred is not a creative force; only love is creative, he is remembered as saying. Where is love asking you to take someone else’s place, even in a small thing?
